- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), often underestimating true values by 5–10%.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true decline.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility — forecasts spike after minor price movements (e.g., 0.5–1.5% change) that don’t warrant a large adjustment.
- Model underestimates the “tail risk” — fails to anticipate sudden drops in the final 5–7 days, especially when true values drop below 55–60.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates short-term price swings and overestimates long-term trends.
- Forecasts often misalign with the “mean reversion” pattern — model holds onto high values longer than actual market behavior suggests.
